name: react-doctor
description: Your agent writes bad React. This catches it
readmeExcerpt: React Doctor runs deterministic checks on your code. It reports issues in state and effects, performance, architecture, security, accessibility, and maintainability. Supports React projects built with Next.js, Vite, Astro, TanStack, React Native, and Expo. [Documentation →](https://react.doctor/docs) ## Install ### 1. Run a scan Run this command from your project root: ```bash npx react-doctor@latest ``` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07cc88d9-9589-44c3-aa73-5d603cb1c570 ### 2. Install for agents Install the skill to help your coding agent find and fix React issues: ```bash npx react-doctor@latest install ``` Supports coding agents including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode. ### 3. Run in CI Scan each pull request and report the issues it introduces: ```bash npx react-doctor@latest ci install ``` [CI docs →](https://react.doctor/ci) ### 4. Configure rules Choose rules and scan settings in `doctor.config.ts`. With `customRulesOnly: true`, explicit `rules` settings of `"warn"` or `"error"` enable selected ported rules. Legacy rule names also work. Other ported rules and the React Compiler plugin stay off. [Configuration docs →](https://react.doctor/docs/configuration/config-files) ## Runtime performance traces Record a Chrome DevTools performance trace while you interact with a running React app: ```bash npx react-doctor@latest scan http://localhost:3000 ``` [Runtime trace docs →](https://react.doctor/docs/reference/cli-reference#runtime-performance-traces) ## Telemetry The CLI collects crash reports and anonymous usage data. See [Data use](https://react.doctor/docs/legal/data-use) for details. To opt out, run: `npx react-doctor@latest --no-telemetry` ## Contributing [Report an issue](https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor/issues) MIT-licensed

releases.name: react-doctor@0.9.17
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- [#1864](https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor/pull/1864) [`fcfb6ea`](https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor/commit/fcfb6ea06717886c210bac1c93cf1c154076af76) Thanks [@aidenybai](https://github.com/aidenybai)! - Fix false new findings in `--baseline` and `--scope changed` after formatting or editing existing flagged code. Compare finding counts per file and rule, then use fingerprints, messages, and Git line shifts to identify added findings. Skip location matching when counts do not increase. Apply portable config filters to saved baseline findings and reject reports with missing or incompatible source-dependent filter settings; regenerate those base reports with the current version and settings.

- Updated dependencies []:
  - oxlint-plugin-react-doctor@0.9.17

readmeHtml:
React Doctor runs deterministic checks on your code. It reports issues in state and effects, performance, architecture, security, accessibility, and maintainability.

Supports React projects built with Next.js, Vite, Astro, TanStack, React Native, and Expo.

Documentation →

Install

1. Run a scan

Run this command from your project root:

npx react-doctor@latest
Main.mp4

2. Install for agents

Install the skill to help your coding agent find and fix React issues:

npx react-doctor@latest install

Supports coding agents including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode.

3. Run in CI

Scan each pull request and report the issues it introduces:

npx react-doctor@latest ci install

CI docs →

4. Configure rules

Choose rules and scan settings in doctor.config.ts.

With customRulesOnly: true, explicit rules settings of "warn" or "error" enable selected ported rules. Legacy rule names also work. Other ported rules and the React Compiler plugin stay off.

Configuration docs →

Runtime performance traces

Record a Chrome DevTools performance trace while you interact with a running React app:

npx react-doctor@latest scan http://localhost:3000

Runtime trace docs →

Telemetry

The CLI collects crash reports and anonymous usage data. See Data use for details.

To opt out, run: npx react-doctor@latest --no-telemetry

Contributing

Report an issue

MIT-licensed

aiSummary.oneLiner: Static analysis tool that deterministically scans React codebases for performance, security, and architecture issues.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: React Doctor is a specialized linting and static analysis tool designed specifically for React applications. It scans codebases to identify common pitfalls introduced by developers or AI coding agents. The tool focuses deterministically on state management, effect lifecycles, performance bottlenecks, and architectural anti-patterns. By operating purely through static analysis, it provides immediate feedback without requiring the application to be running or tests to be written. It helps maintain code quality and catch subtle bugs before they reach production.
keyFeatures: Deterministic scanning: Reliably identifies issues without relying on dynamic execution or flaky tests.
React-specific rules: Targets unique React anti-patterns involving hooks, state, and the component lifecycle.
Performance bottleneck detection: Flags inefficient rendering patterns or excessive re-renders.
AI-agent auditing: Catches common hallucinated or syntactically poor React code generated by AI assistants.
Security vulnerability checks: Identifies potential security flaws specific to frontend React architectures.

useCases.title: Auditing AI-generated code
useCases.description: Run the tool on pull requests created by AI agents to ensure they follow React best practices.

useCases.title: Improving application performance
useCases.description: Identify and refactor components that cause unnecessary re-renders or block the main thread.

useCases.title: Enforcing team standards
useCases.description: Integrate the scanner into CI/CD pipelines to prevent bad architectural patterns from being merged.

useCases.title: Upgrading legacy codebases
useCases.description: Scan older React projects to systematically find and fix outdated lifecycle patterns.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This tool is for frontend developers, technical leads, and teams heavily utilizing React. It is especially useful for teams augmenting their workflow with AI agents, ensuring the generated code meets strict quality standards.
